introduction_markdown:
**GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD - General Certificate of Education Examination. JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL. English Language, Paper 2 (0730).**

Answer your questions either exclusively from **PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS)** or from **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS)**.

**PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS) - Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours.** Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION (Section A: Composition, Section B: Prescribed Texts, Section C: Creative Writing). ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - Duration: Three Hours.** Instructions to candidates: Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - SECTION B: COMPOSITION (20 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (06 marks); Expression (08 marks); Accuracy (06 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write about from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 500 and 550 words.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: what marriage is and its forms in Cameroon.
2. Its purposes: companionship, children, economic benefits, unity of families.
3. The problems: money, communication, infidelity, in-laws, differences.
4. The consequences of failed marriages.
5. Conditions for success: preparation, respect, honesty, forgiveness, shared duties.
6. Conclusion.

**Model composition (525 words)**

Marriage is the lawful union of a man and a woman who promise to live together, to love and to support each other, usually with the aim of founding a family. It is one of the oldest institutions of human society, and in Cameroon it takes several forms: the traditional ceremony in which families exchange gifts, the civil wedding at the town hall, and the religious blessing in church or mosque. Although it is a source of joy, it is also a serious commitment that requires preparation.

The purposes of marriage are many. First, it offers companionship: two people share their joys and sorrows, so that neither has to face the difficulties of life alone. Second, it provides a stable framework for bearing and raising children, who need the love, discipline and protection of both parents. Third, it brings economic benefits, because a couple can pool their incomes and build property together. Finally, it unites two families and strengthens the bonds of the community, which explains why weddings are celebrated with songs, dances and feasting.

Nevertheless, many marriages today are in trouble. A major cause is money. Some young couples spend large sums on a luxurious wedding that they cannot afford and begin their life in debt. Others quarrel constantly because of unemployment or because one partner earns far more than the other. Another cause is poor communication. Husbands and wives who do not talk honestly about their feelings allow small misunderstandings to grow into bitter resentment. Infidelity destroys trust more quickly than any other fault, and the interference of in-laws can make matters worse. In addition, differences in religion, education or ambition, which were ignored during courtship, appear after the wedding.

The consequences of failed marriages are painful. Divorce leaves children confused and sometimes deprived of a parent's care, and the former partners may suffer loneliness, shame and financial hardship. For this reason, society should help couples to build marriages that last.

What, then, makes a marriage succeed? Preparation is the first condition. Young people should choose partners for their character and values and not only for their beauty or wealth, and they should take time to know each other's family and habits. Counselling by pastors, imams or elders can help them to discuss money, children and responsibilities before they take their vows. Respect and honesty are the second condition. A husband and wife should speak truthfully, listen patiently and share decisions. Finally, forgiveness is necessary, because no two human beings are perfect and every couple will face storms. Both partners should also share domestic duties and financial planning, because the old idea that the home belongs only to the woman and the money only to the man no longer suits a world in which both often work.

In conclusion, marriage is a noble institution that can bring happiness, security and growth, but it is neither a fairy tale nor a mere ceremony. It demands maturity, sacrifice and a love that is renewed every day. Those who enter it with open eyes, and who work together with patience, will find that the home they build becomes the foundation of a strong and happy society.

**Marking grid (the paper prints the split of the 20 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 6 | A relevant treatment of the topic as set, a clear introduction, paragraphs that each develop one idea, a logical order and a conclusion |
| Expression | 8 | Varied sentence structures, precise vocabulary, suitable register and tone, good use of linking words, a convincing style |
| Accuracy | 6 | Correct grammar, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing fewer than 500 or more than 550 words, or ignoring the topic's exact wording (for example listing points instead of telling a story, or giving only one side when asked 'Do you agree?').
2. A weak plan: a long introduction, paragraphs that repeat one idea, no conclusion; or a pre-prepared composition that does not fit the question (it earns no marks).
3. Treating the one-word topic 'Marriage' as a licence to write about anything: the essay needs a clear line (what marriage is, its value, its problems, how to succeed).
